rows.statutoryAuthority: s. 165.83(2) Wis. Stats.; Wisconsin Department of Justice, Crime Information Bureau form DJ-LE-247 (2/17)
rows.componentsNote: primary_filing is the rendered form; filing_instructions is participant-instructions.md; record_discrepancy_analysis is reports/record-discrepancy-analysis.json, which sets out the six discrepancies DJ-LE-247 recognises and what the form itself says each one requires.
notableDecisions: The requester's name is NOT written, and that is the substantive decision in this family. The box is captioned "(Last, First, Middle, Suffix)" and the platform holds the name in natural order; writing it as held would put the first name where the Bureau reads a surname. On a form whose whole subject is a record matched to the wrong person, that is a different name rather than a differently written one. It is recorded in the field map under factsHeldButNotWritable — a fact held and not writable, not a fact absent — and the instructions give it its own section.

The subject's date of birth IS written, under a caption asking for mm/dd/yy, in the ISO form the platform holds. The two decisions differ on purpose: a date in ISO order is the same date to any reader, a name in the wrong order is not the same name. The format difference is disclosed to the participant, put to the visual reviewer, and raised against the shared finalizer, which formats no dates at all.

Every write box is a measured table cell — four strokes, each divider required to run at least 80% of the cell — and the TOP of each box is measured too, three points under the lowest printed line inside the cell. That last part is not decoration: one caption on this form wraps to two lines and its second line sits exactly where a constant offset would put the value. The cell it belongs to is recorded as too shallow to write in, and the build asserts no cell it writes to is one of those.

The baseline sits four points above the cell's bottom rule rather than the shared finalizer's two. Two is right for a value on a printed underline; in a table cell the rule is the border and a descender crossing it reads as ink in the cell below. The first raster of this family showed exactly that on an e-mail address, and it was fixed before the family was returned.

None of the six challenge reasons is ticked. Which one applies is the substance of the challenge and the platform does not hold it — and the tick boxes are not strokes in the content stream in any event, so there is no measured box to mark. Both are true; the first is the operative reason.

Page 2 of the form is the Bureau's own statement that state law does not permit the removal of arrest or disposition information, only the addition of notations in three named cases. It is quoted verbatim under its own heading in the instructions, because a participant arriving here expecting removal is at the wrong route.
findingsRaisedForOthers: ADVISORY, owner scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-official-form-finalize.mjs: the finalizer formats no dates — its only normalisation is stripping whitespace — so a caption that names a date format cannot be honoured. DJ-LE-247 asks for mm/dd/yy and gets ISO.

The corpus files DJ-LE-247 under 04_SUPPORTING_PROCESS with assetClass SUPPORT and revision REV-UNKNOWN, although the form prints "DJ-LE-247 (2/17)" on its face and is the operative challenge form for this route. Resolved by state and form number; binds by exact SHA-256; raised for the owner of the corpus index.

This page's tick boxes are not strokes in the content stream, the same as DJ-LE-250B in PF11. Two Wisconsin DOJ forms now show that split — table rules found normally, tick boxes not found at all — so a zero from checkboxCandidates on a Wisconsin DOJ form is not evidence that there is no box.

BLOCKING for the raster gate, owner of the packet-factory builder contract: assembled packet PDFs are NOT byte-reproducible. PDFDocument.create() stamps /CreationDate and /ModDate from the wall clock, and save({updateMetadata:false}) stops those being refreshed but not being set. Two builds of identical inputs were measured differing in exactly six bytes, all of them timestamp digits. A RASTER_PASS bound to one build's SHA-256 is therefore invalidated by a rebuild that changed nothing, which is the opposite of what a hash-bound gate is for. The fix is two lines before save: setCreationDate(new Date(0)) and setModificationDate(new Date(0)). This lane applied it to the three families no VF lane has been assigned, and proved reproducibility by rebuilding and comparing. It did NOT apply it to its earlier families: VF-SRC-A and VF-SRC-B are reading those now, and moving bytes under a verifier mid-read is worse than leaving a known non-determinism in place for the Captain to sequence.
